text:
Landed. DataTable went from 19 accessors to four — names, contains, column, get[A] — with ColumnType instances carrying typeName and extraction, so the Ints-widen-to-Doubles rule lives in one instance. Lookups take a ColumnId, so a caller must have parsed a name before it can ask.

Five dead throwing twins went with them: resolveSeconds, resolveNumericVector, resolveHrf, resolveHrfBasis, raiseStrictDiagnostics, and TableEnv.resolve — all private and unreferenced, the residue of the two-tier convention applied to operations. Across design main, *Either methods dropped from 44 to 36.

Two callers became total on the way: CovariateSpec.construct now returns Either (row mismatch is InvalidSchedule, column problems come from get), and GroupDesign's covariate reader distinguishes a missing column from a non-numeric one with one lookup per column instead of two full passes, preserving the missing-before-non-numeric report order.

HrfGenerators keeps a throwing facade over the one accessor, because HrfFun is a total DataTable => HrfSelection with no error channel; EventModelBuilder catches it back into InvalidHrfFun.

design 155 tests, JVM+JS green; compileAll warning-clean.
